explanation: The `-/+` symbol means Terraform will destroy the resource and then recreate it. The `# forces replacement` annotation on the `ami` attribute explains why: AMI cannot be changed in place on a running instance, so the only path to reach the desired state is a destroy-then-recreate cycle. An in-place update (`~`) would leave the instance running; `-/+` does not.

Saving the plan with `-out=tfplan` produces a file that `terraform apply tfplan` will execute exactly as-is. A fresh `terraform apply` (without a plan file) re-runs the plan at apply time, so any change to the configuration or infrastructure between review and apply can produce different actions than what was approved. `-auto-approve` still runs a fresh plan; `-refresh=false` skips state refresh but still re-plans.

When every resource in the configuration already matches its real-world state, Terraform reports that no actions need to be taken and the summary shows zeros in all three counts. This is not an error — it means the infrastructure is already in the desired state. A missing state file would cause Terraform to propose creating all resources, not a zero-change plan.
